parts.html:
FILL-IN-THE-BLANK · ONE-PAGE FORMAT

Capability Statement — Federal Contractor Editable Template.

HOW TO USE THIS TEMPLATE

Replace every [BRACKETED] field with your company's information. Print or save as PDF after completing. For an editable digital version, see the Google Docs link in your kit.

COMPANY HEADER BLOCK
Company Legal Name [YOUR COMPANY NAME, LLC / INC / LLP]
Website [www.yourcompany.com]
CAGE Code [5-character CAGE]
UEI [12-character Unique Entity ID]
DUNS (legacy) [9-digit DUNS, if applicable]
Primary NAICS [Code] — [Description]
Additional NAICS [Code], [Code], [Code]
PSC Codes [Code] — [Description]

Core Competencies.

List four to six specific capabilities. Be precise — 'IT support' is weak. 'Tier 2 helpdesk supporting 10,000-user enterprise networks' is strong.

Competency 1[Specific capability with measurable detail]
Competency 2[Specific capability with measurable detail]
Competency 3[Specific capability with measurable detail]
Competency 4[Specific capability with measurable detail]
Competency 5[Specific capability with measurable detail]
Competency 6[Specific capability with measurable detail]

Differentiators.

Three reasons an agency should choose you over every other contractor in your space. Be concrete. No buzzwords.

1. [What makes you uniquely capable — a proprietary process, specialized team, unique certification, or speed advantage.]

2. [Your track record that directly applies to federal work — specific outcomes, clearance levels, past agency experience.]

3. [A client or mission-impact proof point — not generic praise, a real result with numbers.]

Past Performance.

Three to five contracts that prove you can deliver. List federal first, then commercial. POC line should be a real human a contracting officer can call.

Agency / Client Contract # Value Period NAICS POC
[Agency Name] [Contract #] [$XXX,XXX] [MM/YY–MM/YY] [NAICS] [Name, Phone]
[Agency Name] [Contract #] [$XXX,XXX] [MM/YY–MM/YY] [NAICS] [Name, Phone]
[Agency Name] [Contract #] [$XXX,XXX] [MM/YY–MM/YY] [NAICS] [Name, Phone]
[Commercial Client] N/A [$XXX,XXX] [MM/YY–MM/YY] [NAICS] [Name, Phone]

Certifications & Socioeconomic Status.

Check every status that applies. Keep this section current — agencies search SAM by certification, and a missed checkbox costs you set-aside opportunities.

Small Business (SB)[ ] Check if applicable
SDVOSB / VOSB (Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned)[ ] Check if applicable
8(a) Business Development[ ] Check if applicable
HUBZone[ ] Check if applicable
WOSB / EDWOSB (Women-Owned)[ ] Check if applicable
ISO 9001:2015 Certified[ ] Check if applicable
CMMC Level [X][ ] Check if applicable
Other: [Certification][ ] Check if applicable

Point of Contact.

One person. Direct line. The contracting officer should never have to figure out who to call.

Name [Full Name, Title] Phone [Direct line]
Email [email@company.com] Address [Street, City, State ZIP]
FIELD TIP

Save the finished file as [Company]_Capability_Statement_[YYYY-MM].pdf. Refresh the date stamp every quarter, even if nothing else changes. Old date stamps signal a dead vendor.

parts.headline: A capability statement is a door opener, not a contract.
parts.body: Fill in this template, send it to a contracting officer, then move to the next play in the kit — the Sources Sought response. CapturePilot drafts both for you in about ten minutes, with your CAGE, UEI, and past performance pre-populated.
